finding: `taskflow close` stages the whole planning task-card file when writing closure frontmatter. If the same physical card file also contains an unrelated in-flight planning edit, the close commit can forcibly include that edit because there is no partial-stage or field-scoped closeback path.
expectedBehavior: Planning closeback should stage only the closure mutation or provide a governed split/reconcile path when a physical planning card has unrelated dirty hunks. It should fail with a precise diagnostic rather than silently coupling close metadata with unrelated planning changes.
evidenceOrRepro: TASK-AAO-0206 governed close produced planning commit `cca6b591ebdef1970f8110be0c6568f5eb9c2dfe`; the commit necessarily included both closure fields and a separate `TASK-AAO-0068` relationship edit from `depends_on` to `softRelations` in the same task-card file.
followUp: Add closeback partial-stage support or a planning-card hunk isolation check. Include a regression where closure metadata and unrelated frontmatter/body edits coexist in one card.
